subject: biology
title: Ecology Adventure 2: Carbon and nitrogen cycles
welcome_lead: Today you'll cycle carbon and nitrogen through the biosphere.
meta_desc: Biology — carbon cycle, nitrogen cycle, fixation, nitrification, denitrification, biogeochemistry.
final_note: You learned carbon moves via photosynthesis, respiration and combustion, and nitrogen requires bacteria to be fixed, nitrified and returned.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Carbon stores: atmosphere (CO₂ ~420 ppm 2023), oceans (HCO₃⁻), biomass, fossil fuels, limestone.

Fluxes: photosynthesis pulls CO₂ out; respiration, combustion, decomposition release it.

Atmospheric CO₂ has risen from 280 ppm (pre-industrial) due to fossil fuel burning + deforestation — driving climate change.

78% of air is N₂ — but unreactive. Bacteria do the heavy lifting:

- Nitrogen-fixing (Rhizobium in root nodules of legumes): N₂ → NH₃.
- Nitrifying (Nitrosomonas, Nitrobacter): NH₃ → NO₂⁻ → NO₃⁻ (plant-usable).
- Denitrifying (Pseudomonas in waterlogged soils): NO₃⁻ → N₂.

Industrial Haber process fixes 100+ Mt N/year — more than all natural fixation combined.

Fertiliser runoff causes eutrophication: NO₃⁻ → algal bloom → death → bacterial decay → O₂ depletion → fish kill.

Gulf of Mexico 'dead zone' from Mississippi runoff is a global case study.
